scope: A disposable Kind v1.36.1 cluster verifies native namespace quota, selected tenant and platform RBAC, and the pinned Kueue v0.17.7 controller's quota, readiness-timeout, and named tenant workload-priority behavior. A case-owned timeout Job's exact Workload UID and raw requeue state are captured before foreground cleanup because the pinned controller has a global PodsReady gate. Separate CPU-only LocalQueues demonstrate sampled historical-use ordering with Admission Fair Sharing enabled: with equal live priorities and sufficient quota after release, the newer lower-use Workload is admitted first. A distinct ClusterQueue explicitly disables Admission Fair Sharing and uses StrictFIFO; it observes the exact 100m seed admitted, Ready, and completed in its queue while the peer remains unseeded, then observes the older of two equal-priority, seed-matched candidates admitted first after release. These are bounded CPU-only scheduler observations. A third isolated Kueue ClusterQueue enables only within-queue LowerPriority preemption; it observes a 100m victim's eviction by a higher-priority Job and recovery of the same victim Job with a replacement Ready Pod after exact preemptor Job, Workload and owned Pod cleanup. A separate Volcano v1.16.1 fixture verifies the exact controller and scheduler inputs, scoped authorization and a two-worker CPU group held below its Queue capacity requirement and admitted after capacity is raised. A separate namespace verifies that object-count admission counts completed as well as suspended Jobs. Accelerator quotas, representative workload demand and adopted deployments remain distinct evidence requirements.
